Tables 1 and 2 were independently recovered with find_tables. The extraction rules, codebook, screening form including final.open_items and sample_overlap, citation record, both raw extractions, and supplied diff were checked. No research appendix, supplement or data/code link is identified; the Appendix of Algorithmic Contribution in Table 4 is a proposed student deliverable (PDF p. 11, printed p. 189). The saved PDF ends with a truncated reference entry at printed p. 190. The supplied diff contains repeated count-field entries; each distinct study/estimate-field disagreement is resolved once. Neither only_in_a nor only_in_b contains an estimate. Coverage: S1-O1 through S1-O6 each have all three arm comparisons from Table 1; S1-O7 has the same three comparisons for each of the two printed Table 2 metrics. The cosine-similarity and dispersion records use the same submissions and are two representations of one diversity outcome, not independent outcomes or samples. S1-O8 is listed in not_extracted because it has no comparison arm. No eligible estimate missing from both extractors was found. Independent check of agreed core fields: Section 3.1 explicitly describes a randomized between-subjects design with people in three conditions, and Section 8 identifies immediate laboratory output; design_class is lab_rct, assignment_unit is individual and every within_person field is null. Section 3.2 and Table 1 support the study and arm counts; matching allocation and analyzed counts do not establish zero exclusions. Table 1 composite scores and people per arm support participant as the unit and SD level for the six individual-output measures. Neither a two-arm sample total nor a separate observation count is printed for these contrasts; n_total and n_units remain null. Table 2 does not establish the analysis unit, SD level or analysis-specific people counts; these remain null and are not inferred from the test degrees of freedom. Originality is novelty, overall creativity is overall_creativity, appropriateness is usefulness, and the TTCT dimensions are fluency, flexibility and elaboration. Flexibility counts domains within one person and is not across-person diversity (PDF p. 5, printed p. 183, Section 3.4). AI remained available while the scored output was produced in both AI arms; initial unaided ideation preceded AI use and supplies no after_ai outcome (PDF p. 4, printed p. 182, Section 3.1). All six individual-output measures answer with_ai; both across-student similarity/dispersion measures answer across_people. Higher values mean more ideas for fluency, more creative output for the other individual-output dimensions, more similar outputs for cosine similarity, and more diverse outputs for dispersion. No signs are reversed during extraction. Structured Scaffolding is the proposed AI configuration and Unconstrained GenAI Access is the default in every ai_design contrast. The elaboration measure remains null because trained raters are identified without their occupations or domain expertise. No preregistration or cross-paper shared sample is reported. All shared arm means, SDs, p bounds and paper effects were checked against the PDF. The three-arm univariate F tests and eta-squared values remain in outcome notes and Table 1 source quotes, not pairwise test/effect fields. The combined-outcome omnibus MANOVA is also excluded as a two-arm estimate: Section 4.1 prints Pillai’s Trace = 0.941, F(12,946) = 68.34, p < .001, partial η² = .470 (PDF p. 6, printed p. 184). The main-text and abstract conflicts are preserved in notes and open_items. Discussion percentages are retained in percent units without recomputation. No numerical values are read from the ASCII originality-versus-fluency graphic (PDF p. 7, printed p. 185). No arm sums, mean differences, standardized effects, SEs, intervals or transformed dispersion uncertainty were computed. Printed precision and signs, including trailing zeros, are retained in the verbatim PDF quotes. Reconciliation completed 2026-10-11.
